name: ansible
description: Ansible Development Tools: lint, navigator run, execution-environment build, project scaffolding, best-practice prompts

WORKSPACE_ROOT.description: Absolute path to the repo the server may read and write. Set it to the project directory, never to $HOME or /. It bounds FILESYSTEM reach only - see workspace_root_bounds below for what it does NOT bound. Note that nothing in the MCP handshake validates this value: the server connects and enumerates every tool with a nonexistent path (TASK-0017).

workspace_root_bounds.note: WORKSPACE_ROOT is not a blast radius for every destructive tool. Stating it as one - which this manifest did until TASK-0026 - understates real exposure in two places.
bounded: ansible_lint (fix: true): rewrites files, within the workspace
create_ansible_projects: scaffolds directory trees, within the workspace
define_and_build_execution_env: writes execution-environment.yml within the workspace (the container images it builds land in the local image store, which is outside)
not_bounded: ansible_navigator: runs playbooks, which reach REMOTE MANAGED INFRASTRUCTURE. WORKSPACE_ROOT bounds which playbook files the server can read; it bounds nothing about what those playbooks then do to a cluster or a router. Disabled by default - see disabled_tools.
ade_setup_environment: installs OS packages via dnf/apt/brew/pacman, which is SYSTEM-WIDE and outside any workspace

preconditions: Node and npx on PATH. Upstream declares node>=24.0; npm reports EBADENGINE on node 22 but the server runs (npm engines are advisory unless engine-strict is set).

Ansible tooling (ansible-lint, ansible-navigator, ansible-dev-tools) must be installed for the corresponding tools to work. Without it the server still connects and read-only prompt tools work, but environment-dependent tools report a missing dependency rather than failing the connection.
ansible_navigator defaults to containerized execution environments; a working Podman or Docker is needed unless execution environments are disabled.

destructive_tools: ansible_navigator: executes playbooks, which can change real managed infrastructure - DISABLED by default, see disabled_tools
ade_setup_environment: installs OS packages via dnf/apt/brew/pacman and creates virtualenvs
define_and_build_execution_env: writes execution-environment.yml and builds container images
ansible_lint (fix: true): rewrites playbook files in place
create_ansible_projects: scaffolds directory trees on disk

disabled_tools.note: ADVISORY ONLY. Nothing enforces this: the upstream server exposes every tool and this repo cannot switch one off. Disablement is carried out by the per-client wiring in configs/*/README.md, which instruct a reader not to enable it - and a user can re-enable it in their own client config at any time. tests/validate.sh does NOT check this field, and deliberately: the manifest schema has no enabled-tool concept, and a key nothing verifies is a claim nothing enforces. Listed here so the reason travels with the manifest rather than living only in three client snapshots.

tools.reason: It cannot express the safe workflow while it can execute against production. Its parameters are userMessage, filePath, mode, environment, disableExecutionEnvironment - no inventory, no limit, no --check, no --diff (verified by live tool enumeration, PLAN-0003 finding F5, re-verified 2026-09-15). So it cannot perform a change preview or scope a run. The control venv's own ansible-playbook does everything this tool does and everything it cannot. A second reason worth recording: userMessage is a natural-language string the server parses to locate the playbook, so invocation is LLM-message-parsed rather than schema-pinned - the determinism argument for MCP does not hold for this tool.
